Let me analyze the video frames:

1. 0.000s: A 3D LEGO brick editor. Light gray environment, a studded baseplate (light gray), a red 2×2 brick placed, a yellow 2×2 preview brick (semi-transparent) hovering where the mouse is. Left side has three circular buttons (top: black with a brick+hammer icon "build mode", middle: move/pan icon, bottom: eraser icon). Bottom toolbar: undo, redo, | color swatches (red, orange, yellow, green, light blue, blue, purple, dark gray/black, rainbow color picker), | width select (2), swap icon, depth select (2), | folder (open), save, play, trash (red). Top-right mute icon.

2. 3.000s: Yellow preview over the red brick — stacking. The preview is semi-transparent yellow positioned above/on the red brick. Green selected in toolbar (highlighted swatch).

3. 8.000s: Green 2×2 bricks placed on top (green 2x2 at a level above red), red brick partially visible below. Another yellow preview at right.

4. 12.000s: Width dropdown open showing options 1-6, "Width (...)" tooltip, width "3" highlighted. More green placed.

5. 15.000s: Width 3, purple color selected; yellow 3-wide preview. Toolbar shows "3" width now.

6. 18.000s: Purple 3×2 brick placed on top. Camera has changed (looking from different angle). Pause icon "||" at bottom center — this is the play/pause showcase mode? Actually there's a pause button at bottom center of the screen. The toolbar is hidden. Hmm, interesting: at 18s the UI toolbar and left buttons are hidden and there's a pause icon at bottom center. This may be a "presentation/showcase mode" that plays a camera orbit animation, with a pause button. The camera angle differs (rotated view).

7. 23.000s: Back to editor UI (toolbar visible), hovering over the swap button with tooltip "Swap (s)". Purple selected.

8. 25.000s: After swap — width 2, depth 3. Preview yellow 2 wide × 3 deep placed over purple brick area. The purple brick below now has 2×3? Actually the purple brick got... hmm, the swap button swaps width and depth. The preview shows 2-wide, 3-deep.

9. 29.000s: More purple/green bricks, camera rotated.

10. 32.000s: Camera rotated more (manual orbit) — view from another angle, toolbar visible, mode buttons grayed except... At 32s the left buttons are dimmed and eraser appears black-ish? Actually the middle button is dark. Hmm, at 32s: left icons look dim/disabled (dark background). This might be "manual camera mode" active where the middle button is selected (black). The scene shows bricks from a rotated top view.

11. 38.000s: Clear Set dialog: dark overlay, white card, "Clear Set" title, X close, "Are you sure you want to clear the entire set? This action cannot be undone." Cancel and Clear (red) buttons. The scene behind is dimmed.

12. 40.000s: Empty baseplate after clear. Toolbar visible.

So the interactions:
- Build mode: click on baseplate or brick → place brick at grid-snapped position with preview following mouse. Preview is semi-transparent brick of current color, size = width × depth (studs).
- Stacking: clicking on top of an existing brick places new brick on top (y level +1).
- Adjacent placement: click next to a brick on the baseplate.
- Color selection: swatches.
- Width/depth selects: 1-6 options. Swap button swaps width/depth.
- Play mode: hides UI, shows pause button, camera slowly orbits (showcase). Pause returns to editor.
- Manual camera mode: middle-left button; drag to orbit camera. (Or in build mode, right-drag orbits too maybe.)
- Erase mode: bottom-left button; hovering highlights target brick (red?), click deletes.
- Clear button → dialog; Cancel/X keeps, Clear removes all.

Also mute icon top-right (static). Undo/redo buttons (not scored, static ok). Open/save (static). Rainbow color button — custom color; not scored but could implement simple prompt or leave static. I'll make the rainbow button open a native color input maybe — simple. But spec says custom color popup not scored; can keep static icon. I might implement a simple color input to be safe? "界面 上可保留其静态图标" — fine to keep static. I'll implement it as a hidden color input trigger — minimal effort, but not necessary. Let me just make it a button that opens <input type="color"> and sets custom color. That's cheap and harmless.

Design details:
- Environment: light gray marble-ish background. I can generate a canvas texture with noise/marble veins, or just a light gray color with subtle texture. Use a large plane or scene.background + fog. The marble has veins; I can procedurally draw a marble texture on a canvas. Keep it simple: canvas 512² with light gray + white noise + faint veins.
- Baseplate: a big studded plate (approx 32×32 studs?) light gray, slightly darker than the floor, with studs (cylinders). In the video the plate appears semi-translucent light gray-lavender with studs. The studs on the plate look like small cylinders. The plate has a subtle shadow. Plate color ~ #c9c7d4, floor ~ #d6d4de with marble veins.
- The plate is big: roughly 40 studs across. Studs visible as small bumps.

Bricks: LEGO brick with studs on top. Brick unit: 1 stud = 8mm; height = 9.6mm. Use unit U = 1 (stud spacing), brick height H = 1.2*U? Actually 9.6/8 = 1.2. Use U=1, H=1.2, brick slightly smaller footprint than stud spacing? Real bricks are 7.8mm wide per stud (0.2mm gap). I'll render body width = U*0.98 or just U with tiny gap. For visuals, brick body with studs radius ~0.3U, height ~0.18U.

Materials: MeshStandardMaterial with roughness ~0.3, slight clearcoat (physical). Colors: red #d3242b-ish (#c91a09), orange #ff8800? video orange #f5a623-ish, yellow #ffd500/#f7d117, green #237841/#2e8b3d (video green looks like #3f9b45), light blue #68c3e8/#7fd0ec, blue #2f6fce/#4787d8, purple #7b2fa8/#8a2be2 (video purple #5c2d91-ish), dark gray #3a3a3c, black swatch #1e1e1e? The 8th swatch is dark gray. Rainbow = custom.

In video frame 0, selected red swatch has a white ring around it (selected indicator). Selected swatch gets a white ring/scale.

UI Layout:
- Left top: three circular buttons stacked vertically at ~16px margin, 44-48px diameter, gap ~12px. First: black bg, white brick-with-wrench icon (build). Second: gray translucent bg with move arrows icon (camera/manual view). Third: gray translucent bg with eraser icon (erase). Active mode = black bg. At 32s, all three look dim — maybe because they're disabled during... hmm at 32s the left buttons look faded (dark gray on dark). Possibly because in manual view mode they fade out? Frame 32 shows middle dark? Hard to tell. Let me simplify: active button black, inactive translucent gray.

Actually at 32.000s: all three left buttons appear dark gray/faded. The scene is in a rotated camera view. Maybe this is during "play/showcase" fade? No, toolbar is visible. Could be the screenshot captured a transition. I'll not overthink.

- Bottom toolbar: centered, rounded-full (border-radius ~24px), dark (#1b1d21 / near-black), height ~52px, contains: undo, redo, separator, 8 color swatches (28px circles) + rainbow button, separator, width select (dark rounded rect with chevron), swap icon, depth select, separator, folder icon, save icon, separator, play icon, trash icon (red).

Tooltips: "Swap (s)" on hover over swap; "Width (...)" tooltip near width select. I'll add title-like custom tooltips for swap ("Swap (s)") and maybe width/depth. Keyboard shortcut 's' swaps.

- Selects: native <select> styled dark with options 1-6. In the video, opening width shows a white dropdown panel with numbers 1-6, current highlighted. Native select does that.

- Play mode: clicking play hides toolbar + left buttons, shows pause icon at bottom center (two vertical bars, dark). Camera orbits slowly around the model. Click pause → return to build UI, camera stays where it is (or returns). In the video at 18s during play mode the camera angle is different and rotated. Then at 23s back in edit UI with camera still rotated. So play/pause just toggles UI + orbit; camera position persists.

- Manual camera mode (middle button): drag anywhere orbits the camera (rotate + zoom via wheel). In build mode, dragging on empty space might also orbit? To keep modes clear: in camera mode, left-drag orbits, wheel zooms; clicks don't place bricks. In build mode, left click places; maybe dragging also orbits with right mouse? Simpler: in build mode, left-drag rotates too? That conflicts with placement clicks. Common approach: build mode click places brick; drag (movement > threshold) orbits camera. I'll implement: pointerdown records; if moved > 5px → treat as orbit (any mode except erase where drag could multi-delete? keep simple: orbit allowed in all modes via drag, click places/deletes). That matches "手动改变视角" requirement plus mode separation. And the middle button toggles "camera mode" where click doesn't place.

Hmm, but requirement 6: "清楚区分放置模式、手动视角模式和擦除模式" — clearly distinguish modes. So: build mode: click places, drag orbits (fine). Camera mode: clicks do nothing but drag orbits. Erase mode: hover highlights brick red, click deletes.

- Erase highlight: hovered brick gets emissive/red tint. In video I didn't see explicit erase usage but requirement says implement. Highlight = make it reddish or lighten. I'll set emissive to red-ish and maybe opacity.

- Placement preview: semi-transparent brick (opacity ~0.5) of selected color, follows mouse via raycast onto baseplate top surface and brick tops. Position snapped to grid. When hovering over existing brick top, y = that brick's top level. Also adjacent placement: raycast to baseplate gives ground level. Overlap check: if preview would intersect existing brick, maybe tint red? Video shows preview overlapping existing bricks when stacking (it's on top). Keep simple: allow placement at snapped cell; if occupied at that level, find top height at target cells and place on top (stacking). Actually better: raycast determines the surface clicked: if hit a brick, place at hitY + 1 level; if hit plate, place at level 0. Then check occupancy: if occupied at that level (e.g., clicking on the side of a tall brick?), bump to top of stack at those cells. Simple approach: compute target level = max top over footprint cells of the snap position derived from raycast, but at least the hit-based level. Hmm.

Let me design: brick occupies grid cells [gx, gx+w) × [gz, gz+d) at level ly (ly = integer, height = ly*H). Occupancy map: Map "x,z" → list of levels or just top level + per-level set. For placement:
- Raycast against bricks' top faces and plate. Determine cell under cursor: from raycast point, cell = floor(point.x + 0.5)? Let's use snapping: world x → stud coordinate s = round(x / U - (w-1)/2)? For a w-wide brick, center offset so cursor is inside footprint: gx = round(px/U - w/2) etc. Simpler: gx = Math.round(px/U - w/2); gz = Math.round(pz/U - d/2). Then footprint cells.
- If the ray hit a brick B at point p: candidate level = B.level + 1. But if the cursor is near the brick edge, the footprint may extend beyond; that's fine (cantilever allowed? video shows green 3x2 overhanging? At 8s green bricks overhang the red — yes at 8s a green 2x2 sits half on red half on plate? Looks like green at level 1 partially overhanging). We allow floating/overhang (spec says no悬空支撑规则 needed).
- Compute placement level = max over footprint cells of (top[cell]) but at least hitLevel? Hmm: If clicking on plate next to a brick whose cell overlaps footprint... e.g., placing 3-wide next to a 2x2 could overlap that brick's cells. Real behavior (video 15s): yellow 3-wide preview overlapping existing green brick — placed on top of green? At 15s the yellow preview is at the same level as the green top? The green 3x2 at level... Let me look: at 15s, yellow preview is placed overlapping green brick and red brick; its top appears at the green top level +? It looks like it sits on top spanning green and empty space at green's top+1. Actually the preview's bottom edge aligns with green brick's mid-height... The preview at 15s looks like it's at level 2 (on top of green which is level 1). Whatever — simplest robust rule: target level = max(top of each footprint cell) (0 if empty), except when ray hit a brick's side? Fine: level = max over cells of topHeight[cell]; if ray hit a brick and its top level +1 > that max, use hitTop+1. Actually max over cells ≥ hit brick top +1 already (since hit brick is under footprint? only if footprint covers its cells). Edge case: ray hits brick side, footprint cells don't include hit brick's column → level could be lower, causing intersection with the hit brick itself. To avoid intersections: level = max(maxCellTop, hitBrick.topLevel + 1 if hit brick). Also clamp to ≥ 0.

Wait, but in the video, bricks are placed adjacent sharing the same level: e.g., at 0s the yellow is next to red on the plate at level 0. Clicking plate next to red with 2-wide footprint that doesn't overlap red cells → level 0. Good.

Stacking: click on top of red → footprint covers red cells → level 1. Good.

If footprint partially overlaps a taller brick, level = that top → sits on top partially cantilevered. Fine.

Occupancy: keep Map cell→maxTop and per-cell set of levels for delete. Delete just removes that brick and recompute tops. No gravity.

- Shadow: directional light with shadows; bricks cast shadows on plate; plate casts on floor. Video shows soft shadows to the left of bricks (light from right/top). Plate shadow visible on marble floor.

Now visuals: To match: light environment, ambient + hemisphere + directional. Renderer: antialias, shadowMap PCFSoft, toneMapping ACES? Colors in video are fairly saturated but soft. Use outputColorSpace SRGB.

Studs on plate: 40×40 = 1600 cylinders — could be instanced mesh. Use InstancedMesh for plate studs. Brick studs: each brick has w*d studs; use merged geometry per brick or small cylinders per stud (fine, counts low). For performance, create brick body as RoundedBox? Video bricks have sharp edges with slight bevel. Use BoxGeometry with slight scale; studs as cylinders. Could merge into one BufferGeometry per brick using BufferGeometryUtils.mergeGeometries from three/addons. Good.

Plate: big box (thin) + instanced studs. Plate color light lavender-gray #c9c8d6, studs slightly lighter/same. In the video plate studs appear as subtle bumps with pinkish highlights from marble veins — just plain color fine.

Marble floor: large plane with canvas-generated marble texture (light #d8d6e0 with faint white/pink veins). Also use as scene background? The horizon blends — background could be same texture color; use scene.background = color, plus fog to blend. Or make floor huge (400×400) and background color matching average. Video background shows marble veins up to horizon — floor plane huge with texture works with fog to blend into bg color.

Brick geometry: body: width wU*U - gap, depth d*U - gap, height H (1.2U). Studs: cylinder r=0.3U, h=0.17U at each cell center, y = H + studH/2. Brick origin at bottom center. Position y = level*H.

Wait, plate top at y=0; plate thickness below. Bricks at level L occupy y ∈ [L*H, (L+1)*H]. Stud height adds on top.

Preview: same geometry with transparent material (opacity 0.45-0.55, depthWrite false). Color = selected. When invalid (would collide? we always stack so rarely invalid) maybe show anyway.

Erase highlight: change material emissive to 0xff0000*0.35 + slight scale? Keep material per brick instance (clone). Simpler: each brick mesh has its own material (cloned) so highlight easy.

Play mode: hide #toolbar, #modeButtons, show #pauseBtn. Orbit: each frame theta += dt*0.3 around target center of bricks (or plate center). Pause: stop orbit, restore UI.

Toolbar details from frame 0 (1280 wide): toolbar spans x≈243–1032 (≈790px), y≈728–777 (≈50px tall), radius 25. Icons: undo at 277, redo 307, separator ~330, swatches at 360,397,435,473,511,549,587,626 (spacing ~38), rainbow 679, separator ~705, width select box 722–766 (44 wide), swap 787, depth select 806–851, separator ~880, folder 890, save 919, separator ~950, play 965, trash 997.

Selects: dark (#2a2c31?) rounded rect ~44×28, white text "2", chevron. Dropdown opens white panel — native select in dark theme will show white dropdown on most platforms, fine.

Left buttons: at (36,41), (36,101), (36,161) r≈24. First black, others rgba(60,60,65,0.55)?

Mute icon top-right at (1244,37) — static speaker-x icon, white.

Icons: draw with inline SVG. Undo (curved arrow left), redo (curved arrow right), swap (two horizontal arrows ⇄), folder (open folder), save (floppy/disk outline), play (triangle), trash (bin), pause (two bars), move (arrows cross), eraser (diagonal eraser), brick+wrench for build. Trash is red (#e2574c-ish); others white/light gray.

Tooltips: dark small label above toolbar item on hover: "Swap (s)", "Width (studs)", "Depth (studs)". Video shows "Width (...)" tooltip in dark pill above the toolbar at (708,714). And "Swap (s)" dark pill. Implement CSS tooltip via data-tip attr.

Clear dialog: dark overlay rgba(0,0,0,0.55); white card 448×188 at center (x 414–861, y 303–502); title "Clear Set" bold 22px; text gray 14px; X top-right; buttons right-aligned: Cancel (white pill with border/shadow) and Clear (red pill #e4574d, white text).

Now interactions per acceptance: "验收包含原顺序回放以及相同操作的不同位置/颜色/顺序组合" — so evaluation will do: select colors, change width/depth, swap, place multiple bricks, stack, orbit, erase, play/pause, clear dialog cancel/clear. Must all work robustly with pointer events.

Pointer handling: use pointerdown/pointermove/pointerup on renderer canvas. Distinguish click vs drag by movement threshold. Wheel zoom. Right-drag also orbit (prevent context menu). In build mode: on pointerup with small movement and left button → place. In erase: on click over brick → delete. In camera mode: drag orbit only.

Raycasting: against plate top + bricks. For preview, run on pointermove (and after camera moves). Also hide preview when pointer over UI (UI elements are HTML above canvas; pointer events on canvas only fire when not over UI, since UI elements capture). Ensure UI has pointer-events auto and canvas listener attached to canvas element, so moving over toolbar doesn't trigger canvas events. Good.

Grid: plate spans stud coords from -N..N? Let plate be 36×36 studs centered, i.e., cells gx ∈ [-18, 18). U = 1. Plate mesh width 36 (+ a tiny rim?). In video plate looks ~ 40 studs wide with studs across entire plate. Studs count 36×36 = 1296 instances — ok.

Actually measure: at 0s, plate spans roughly x 320→960 (640px) across, studs ~26px apart at center. Screen width 1280. Hard to derive exact stud count; ~24-40. I'll use 36.

Camera: perspective fov ~40, initial position like (0, 14, 22) looking at (0,0,0)? In frame 0, we see plate from a fairly low angle (horizon high, plate occupies middle). Camera slightly above plate, looking down ~30°. Set camera pos (0, 12, 20), target (0, 1.5, 0). Zoom limits radius 8–60. OrbitControls-like custom: implement simple spherical orbit (theta around Y, phi from 0.1..1.4), pan disabled (video only shows rotate/zoom; middle button is "move" icon but let's just orbit; pan optional with shift? skip pan—spec: "手动改变视角" rotate is enough; but icon shows move arrows... I'll implement rotate + wheel zoom; maybe two-button pan skip).

I could just use OrbitControls from three/addons — allowed ("three/addons/..."). OrbitControls gives rotate/zoom; enablePan false. Left-drag rotates — but conflicts with placement clicks: OrbitControls rotates on left drag; click still places on pointerup if no move. That's standard and fine. In camera mode same but clicks don't place. In erase mode OrbitControls also rotates — fine. I'll set controls.enableRotate true always; in build mode clicking without drag places.

But careful: OrbitControls captures pointerdown on canvas; our click detection independent via pointerdown/up distance — fine.

During play mode: disable controls, animate theta by controls or manually rotate camera around target. Simplest: in play mode, each frame controls' autoRotate = true (OrbitControls has autoRotate + autoRotateSpeed, needs controls.update()). Use controls.autoRotate=true speed ~1.0. Pause → autoRotate=false. 

Raycast from camera: use THREE.Raycaster with pointer NDC.

Also handle select change: width/depth 1..6. On change, update preview size. Swap: exchange values, update selects.

Undo/redo: not scored; keep buttons disabled-looking but I can implement simple undo stack cheaply? Not required — leave as static (maybe clickable no-op). Spec says not scored; fine static. But "同一种操作应可重复" — that's about placement ops, not undo. Keep static.

Rainbow button: opens hidden <input type="color">, on change sets a custom color and selects it (ring moves). Cheap, harmless. But is it "custom color popup" (out of scope)? It's fine either way.

Mute icon: static.

Now numbers: The video height H: brick height vs width ratio: 2x2 brick appears roughly square from side (width 2 studs, height ~1.2 stud). Real ratio. Use U=1, H=1.2? Visual at 0s: red brick top face 2x2 studs, side height looks slightly less than stud-width... eh, 1.2 is realistic; video looks about right.

Colors sampling from frames:
- red: #d0202a-ish (bright). I'll use #d31e2c? Video red maybe #cf1f25. Use 0xd3222a.
- orange: #f6a021
- yellow: #f7d21e (bright yellow, preview yellow #f5e04a semi transparent)
- green: #3f9b3f? video green #35953c-ish medium green. Use 0x3d9b44.
- light blue / cyan: #62c9e8
- blue: #4a7fd6
- purple: #7a3bb8? video purple darker #5b2d8e with bright top. Use 0x6d31b8? Frame 18 purple top #5a2ea6, side #7a3fc0 lighter. Standard LEGO purple #a049ce? I'll use 0x7b2fbe... let me pick 0x8137c1? Hmm. Video looks like #6a30a8. Choose 0x7632b4? I'll go with 0x7a3ab8-ish → hex 0x7a3ab8. Fine.
- dark gray: #4a4a4f (the 8th swatch looks charcoal #3f3f46). Use 0x3f3f46.

Plate color: #c9c8d3. Floor marble base #d7d5df.

Lighting: hemisphere (0xffffff, 0xd8d4e0, 0.9), directional (0xffffff, 1.2) from (8, 18, 6) with shadow camera covering plate, shadow radius soft. In video shadows fall to the left (-x) and slightly toward viewer, so light from +x, -z? Shadow of red brick extends left-down in screen. Screen left ≈ world -x when camera at +z. So light from +x. Set dir light position (10, 16, 4).

renderer.toneMapping = ACESFilmic, exposure 1.0; colors will shift slightly but fine. Actually to keep colors close to swatch, use NoToneMapping with sRGB output; standard materials with hemi+dir 1.0 might overexpose. I'll use toneMapping ACES and bump saturation... simpler: outputColorSpace = SRGBColorSpace, toneMapping = NeutralToneMapping (three 0.180 has AgX/Neutral). Neutral keeps colors truer. Use NeutralToneMapping exposure 1.

Marble texture: generate canvas 1024²: fill #d9d7e2, draw ~40 random vein paths (bezier) with rgba(255,255,255,0.5) and rgba(180,175,195,0.25), plus soft blotches pinkish rgba(230,200,210,0.08). Repeat 6×6 over 600×600 plane with anisotropy. Also slight roughness 1.

Plate edge: The plate in video looks like thin sheet with slight border and studs. Add box 36×0.3×36 top at y=0 → center y=-0.15. Studs instanced cylinder r=0.31 h=0.14 at y=0.07? Wait studs must sit on plate top: plate top at y=0? Then bricks sit on plate top → level0 bottom y=0. Studs height 0.14 above plate → bricks would float over studs visually; real bricks hollow under studs—LEGO plate studs go inside brick. Render bricks sitting at y=0 and studs intersecting brick bottoms—fine (hidden). Plate studs visible elsewhere.

Actually in the video, plate studs are clearly visible as bumps. Yes.

Plate maybe slightly translucent (you can see marble veins through it? At 40s the plate looks like frosted glass showing faint color). Use opacity 0.92 transparent? Transparent causes sorting issues with shadows. Keep opaque, color close to floor but slightly more lavender and darker for contrast: #cbc9d6 vs floor #d8d6e0. And add subtle roughness map? Skip.

Shadow: plate receiveShadow, bricks cast+receive, floor receive.

Now the "pause" button during play at 18s: two vertical bars centered bottom (~y=757), dark color, small. Implement div with ‖ icon (SVG two rounded rects), click → pause.

Also during play the toolbar & left buttons hidden (display none) — matches 18s frame.

Edge: after Clear during any camera state — remove all brick meshes, reset occupancy.

Escape key closes dialog too? X button enough.

Keyboard 's' swaps (tooltip says Swap (s)). Add keydown listener (ignore when dialog open).

Now file structure: index.html (all-in-one? or split app.js + style.css). I'll do index.html + css/style.css + js/main.js using import map from vendor. Check initial index.html for import map. Let me read the existing files first.

main.js outline:

```js
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';
import * as BufferGeometryUtils from 'three/addons/utils/BufferGeometryUtils.js';
```

Constants: U=1, H=1.2, PLATE=36 (studs), colors array.

Scene setup, marble canvas texture, plate box + InstancedMesh studs.

Brick factory: buildBrickGeometry(w,d) cached per (w,d): body box (w*U-GAP, H, d*U-GAP) translated y H/2 + studs cylinders at (i - (w-1)/2)*U... positions x = (i - (w-1)/2)*U for i in 0..w-1, z similar; cylinder r=0.3, h=0.22, y = H + 0.11. GAP=0.06? Actually real: 0.2mm/8mm ≈ 0.025U. Use GAP=0.03 → subtle seams. Video bricks have visible seams? Adjacent same-color green bricks show seam line. GAP=0.04.

Brick mesh: geometry cached; material: MeshStandardMaterial({color, roughness:0.35, metalness:0}) clone per brick. castShadow, receiveShadow.

Occupancy: Map key `${x},${z}` → array of levels sorted? Store Map<cellKey, Set<level>> plus per-brick record {id, x,z,w,d,level,mesh,cells}. topOf(x,z): max level+1 in set else 0.
